answer: Neighborhood closure scoring: each agent's trust is capped by how many of its declared peers share peers with it, so a cluster of puppets must weave into the real graph to reach zenith. At least a fixed fraction of an identity's links must close into triangles with distinct, independently aged accounts. Reaching that summit forces the attacker to rent and maintain real social surface per puppet at ongoing cost. Repeat links to velvet-padded shells collapse into one neighborhood, so each extra identity demands fresh, non-overlapping ties.
